10. Fuels
A substance that can supply energy either alone or by reacting with
another substance is known as fuel. Heat produced by fuel is measured in
Calories An ideal fuel should
have high calorific value
(ii) be cheap and easily available
(iii) be easily stored & transport
(iv) be regulated and controlled
(v) have low ignition temperature
The quantity of fuel is expressed in the form of calorific value
Calorific value is the total  quantity of heat liberated by complete
combustion of a unit mass of fuel in air Or oxygen:
Calorific valueof fuels are expressed in kcal / m? or British Thermal unit
(B.T.U) per cubic foot:
kcal/ m] 0.107 B.T.U / ft}
